title: Vote: add an unregister endpoint to the REST spec
summary: rdblue called a vote on adding an unregister endpoint to the REST catalog spec, with the change in PR #16400. Unregister is the opposite of register: it removes a table from a catalog without deleting the underlying data and metadata files, and returns the latest catalog state of the table. The stated purpose is to allow moving a table from one catalog to another, which needs a new endpoint because the files must be left in place. The vote was open for 72 hours. All replies were +1; adutra noted it will be useful for catalog migration, and Maninder Parmar said it defines clearer semantics about data lifecycle. rdblue closed the vote as passed.

positions.stance: Add an unregister endpoint that removes a table from a catalog while leaving its data and metadata files in place, to support moving tables between catalogs.
Supports the endpoint as useful for catalog migration scenarios.
Supports the endpoint because it defines clearer semantics about data lifecycle.

outcome.note: Passed with 16 +1 votes (9 binding, 7 non-binding) and no +0 or -1 votes.

why_it_matters: REST catalogs gain a standard way to drop a table from the catalog without touching its files, which catalog migration tools can rely on.
